Use case: style-transfer / precise-object-edit. This is a replacement background matte for the small stylized platform-game level Custard Creek. The reference supplies ONLY the warm sandstone, muted olive green and jade-water palette. Completely simplify the composition and reduce its scale.
Draw one SMALL ENCLOSED DOWNSTREAM GORGE seen looking down from the top of a waterfall. A quiet jade plunge pool below the viewer flows into ONE short gentle river bend that disappears behind a nearby wooded bank. The whole depicted place is only about 60–100 metres across. Frame that basin with just TWO broad, rounded sandstone bank shapes and a few large, soft masses of willow foliage. Broad readable silhouettes, restrained texture, simple layered rock bands. Softer, stylized game art with low visual noise; calm and uncluttered, matching a warmly lit 3D platformer. Muted warm late-afternoon light, no dramatic sunburst. The back wall and soft tree canopy enclose the scene; only a small pale sky opening at the top if needed. Show the pool far enough below the viewpoint to read as a drop, without exaggerating the depth.
CRITICAL: no vast landscape, no distant mountain ranges, no horizon stretching to infinity, no stacked canyons, no forests of tiny individual trees, no dozens of rock pillars, no multiple waterfalls, no mist, fog banks, spray, smoke or floating particles. No foreground waterfall crest, no nearby ledge or water waves: the game provides its real foreground brink. No characters, text or HUD. Use FEWER, LARGER, QUIETER shapes, with smooth calm water and large soft foliage shapes instead of microdetail. 16:9 landscape. Full bleed; no border.
